title: Assignment 2: Responsive Interactive Web Page (10%) is due
description:
Assignment 2: Responsive Interactive Web Page
Introduction
This assignment is based on:

-    Week 3: CSS Extensions — Responsive & Interactive Design (media queries, content priority, pseudo-elements, hover effects, responsive testing)
-    Week 4: JavaScript Fundamentals (variables, decisions, loops, functions, arrays, objects, basic error handling)

In this assignment, you will build a single-page responsive interactive web page using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

This assignment extends Assignment 1 by adding:

-    Responsive design with media queries
-    Visual interaction using hover and pseudo-elements
-    Basic JavaScript logic and user interaction

________________________________________
Objective
By completing this assignment, you will be able to:

-    Apply responsive design principles using media queries
-    Adjust layout, spacing, and content priority for mobile devices
-    Use pseudo-elements and hover effects for visual feedback
-    Write basic JavaScript using variables, conditions, loops, and functions
-    Update page content dynamically with JavaScript
-    Test your design on different screen sizes

________________________________________
Task 1: Project Setup & Structure (10%)
Create a new folder called: cs230-assignment2

Inside the folder, create three files:

-    index.html
-    style.css
-    script.js

In index.html:

-    Use a correct HTML boilerplate
-    Set <html lang="en">
-    Link style.css and script.js
-    Use semantic layout:
-    <header> (page title and welcome message area)
-    <nav> (navigation links)
-    <main> (main page content with cards/sections)
-    <section> (each content block/card)
-    <footer> (page footer such as copyright, student/course info, last updated, or a short note)

Example footer content ideas (choose one or more):

-    © 2026 Your Name | CS230
-    Last updated: Feb 2026
-    A short note like: This page is for study tracking.

________________________________________
Task 2: Page Content & Layout (HTML + CSS) (25%)
Create a simple Student Dashboard page with the following sections.
Header & Navigation
-    A title: “My Study Dashboard”
-    A navigation bar with three links (they do not need to work):
-    Home
-    Tasks
-    Profile

Layout requirement (Desktop / wide screens):

-    Use Flexbox so the navigation links are arranged horizontally on wide screens.

________________________________________
Main Content Sections
Inside <main>, create three sections (cards).
Each section should be styled as a card using:

-    padding
-    margin (or gap)
-    border
-    border-radius

Layout requirement (Desktop / wide screens):

-    Use Flexbox (or Grid) so that on wide screens the three cards appear side-by-side in one row (horizontal layout).
-    This will make the responsive change in Task 3 clear when switching to mobile.

________________________________________
Section 1 — Profile Card
Include:

-    A heading with your name
-    A short paragraph about your course or interests
-    One profile image with proper alt text

________________________________________
Section 2 — Weekly Goals List
Include:

-    A heading: “Weekly Goals”
-    An unordered list with at least 4 goals

Style the list so it is clear and readable.

________________________________________
Section 3 — Status Panel
Include:

-    A heading: “Study Status”
-    A paragraph with the text: Status: Active

Use a pseudo-element (::after) to display a label such as:

-    ACTIVE (green) or
-    PENDING (orange)

Important: Do not put this label text directly in the HTML.

________________________________________
Task 3: Responsive Design with Media Queries (20%)
Add responsive behavior using media queries.
Requirements
When the screen width is 700px or smaller:

1.    Change the layout so that:

-    The three cards (sections) stack vertically (one under another)
-    Navigation links become vertical instead of horizontal

2.    Adjust readability:

-    Reduce font size slightly
-    Reduce large margins, padding, or gaps

3.    Content priority:

-    Hide one non-important paragraph or image on small screens using CSS
(Example: hide the profile image or an extra “about” paragraph only on small screens.)

________________________________________
Task 4: Hover Effects & Interaction (15%)
Add hover effects to improve usability:

1.    Navigation links:

-    Change color on hover
-    Show underline or background highlight

2.    Profile card:

-    On hover, add a shadow or slight scale effect

________________________________________
Task 5: JavaScript Basics — Dynamic Interaction (25%)
Use script.js to add interactivity.
Part 1 — Welcome Message
At the top of the page, add an empty paragraph:

In JavaScript:

-    Create a variable with your name
-    Use textContent to show: “Welcome, [your name]!”

________________________________________
Part 2 — Study Counter
Add to the Section 3 – Status Panel:

-    A paragraph showing: Study sessions today: 0
-    A button: Add Session
-    A button: Reset

In JavaScript:

-    Create a variable called count
-    Increase count when “Add Session” is clicked
-    Reset count to 0 when “Reset” is clicked
-    Update the paragraph every time

________________________________________
Part 3 — Weekly Goal Checker
Add to the Section 2 – Weekly Goal List:
Create an array in JavaScript with at least 3 goals, for example:

-    "Read notes"
-    "Finish lab"
-    "Practice JavaScript"

Use a loop to:

-    Print all goals to the Console

Add a button: “Show Goals”

When clicked:

-    Display the goals inside a <ul> on the page

________________________________________
Part 4 — Simple Decision
Create a variable: const hoursStudied = 3;

Use if / else to show in the Console:

-    “Good progress” if hoursStudied ≥ 3
-    “You should study more” if hoursStudied < 3

________________________________________
Task 6: Testing & Screenshot Evidence (5%)
Test your page using:

-    Browser resizing
-    DevTools device mode

Take two screenshots:

1.    Desktop view (wide screen)
2.    Mobile view (device mode or narrow window)

Screenshots must show:

-    Navigation
-    At least one card
-    Evidence of responsive layout (cards stacked + nav vertical in mobile)

________________________________________
Deliverables
Submit a ZIP file containing:

-    index.html
-    style.css
-    script.js
-    screenshot-desktop.jpg
-    screenshot-mobile.jpg

________________________________________
Assessment Breakdown
-    Task 1 — Setup & Structure: 10%
-    Task 2 — Content & Layout: 25%
-    Task 3 — Responsive Design: 20%
-    Task 4 — Hover & Pseudo-elements: 15%
-    Task 5 — JavaScript Interaction: 25%
-    Task 6 — Screenshots & Testing: 5%

Total: 100%

________________________________________
Notes
-    Do NOT copy lecture demos directly.
-    Use your own layout and naming.
-    Keep your code simple and readable.
-    Comment your CSS and JavaScript clearly.
-    Late submissions follow the standard module policy.

Assignment 3: Countdown Timer Application (10%) is due
description:
# Assignment 3: Countdown Timer Application

## Introduction

In this assignment, you will create a simple countdown application. The task involves using CSS to design an interface with an apple in the center of the screen, containing an apple and three buttons. These buttons control the start, stop, and pause functionalities of the timer. The timer runs for 1 minute. The timer will change its CSS style after it reaches 15 seconds. After the countdown finished, the clock will alert the user to take a short break.

## Objective

- Develop a basic HTML page featuring a paragraph for displaying the timer, two buttons for controlling the timer, and an apple image as the background.
- Utilise CSS to style the page with a light blue background color, green start button, red stop button, and orange pause button. The timer text should be white by default and turn yellow on hover. When the timer reaches 15 seconds, the text color must change to red.

## Task Description

The tasks outlined below provide detailed steps and requirements to guide you through completing the assignment.

### Task 1: HTML (Hypertext Markup Language) (30%)

Create a basic HTML file with the layout of a countdown timer.

#### Requirements:

- Boilerplate (10%): Implement standard HTML boilerplate code to structure each page, including DOCTYPE, HTML, HEAD, BODY, etc. Make sure the navigation bar at the top of the webpage includes a "Timer" Button.
- Buttons and Timer (10%): Create a paragraph with the id "timer" to display the timer and add buttons for starting, stopping, and pausing the timer.
- Apple Image (10%): Add a background image of apple, you can make it by yourself or download from the website. The apple should be horizontally centred in the webpage.
- You can use this link to remove background for the images:
https://www.remove.bg/
### Task 2: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) (30%)

Style the buttons, timer, and page appropriately for the application using CSS.

#### Requirements:

- Boilerplate (5%): Create a styles.css file and link it to the HTML file. Include a style to make the background of the page a light blue and center the countdown timer on the page.
- Buttons (10%): Style each button with the Roboto font family, white font color. Background color should be green for start, red for stop, and orange for pause. Apply a black border when hovering over each button.
- Apple (15%): The timer text in the apple should be Orbitron font. When hovered over, the timer text should become yellow; otherwise, the timer text should become white. Additionally, when the timer goes below 15 second, change the text color to red and add a background color with rounded corners of 5px to make it stand out from the apple.

### Task 3: JS (JavaScript) (40%)

Implement timer functionality using JavaScript.

#### Requirements:

- Timer (15%): Develop a timer functionality that tracks the time since the start button was pressed. When the timer reaches 0, display an alert to take a break. Pressing the stop button resets the timer, which only starts again when the start button is clicked.
- Pause Button (15%): Implement functionality to pause the timer instead of resetting it. When the pause button is clicked, the text should switch to "Resume", and clicking it again should return to "Pause" while the timer continues running.
- Disable button (10%): Initially, the "Pause" and "Stop" buttons should be disabled and the "start" button should be enabled. After the "Start" button is clicked, the "Pause" and "Stop" buttons should be enabled and the Start" button should be disabled. After "Stop" button is clicked, the three buttons should be reverted back to the intial state (the "Pause" and "Stop" buttons should be disabled and the "Start" button should be enabled).

## Hint:  How to import font in CSS?
https://support.secureprivacy.ai/articles/238540-how-to-add-custom-fonts-using-css-in-secure-privacy-banner

- Use the @import rule: Add the following line at the very beginning of your custom CSS code to import your chosen font:

@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Your+Font+Name&display=swap');

- Replace Your+Font+Name with the actual font name from the font library. For example, Roboto would look like

@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto&display=swap');

**Important**: Always place font imports at the very start of your CSS to ensure they load correctly.

## Deliverables

Submit a .ZIP file to Moodle containing the following items:

- index.html
- styles.css
- script.js
- apple image
- screenshot of application
